Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and a quick note on procurement expectations: 

1) HIPAA: correct — we process PHI for the pilot, so a BAA will be required before any PHI is shared.
2) SOC 2: we are currently operating under SOC 2 Type II readiness; our security team expects the official report to be available in early Aug 2027.
3) Vendor questionnaire: attached is our standard vendor questionnaire; Procurement requires this to be completed for all vendors.
4) Pen test: Procurement/security typically wants evidence of a third-party pen test within the last 12 months. A redacted executive summary is often acceptable for the initial review, but they reserve the right to request more detailed artifacts during contract review.

Can you confirm how Redwood handles:
- Sharing pen test artifacts (executive summary vs full report)
- Vulnerability SLA commitments and typical mitigation windows
- Scan cadence (internal scanning, external scans, third-party pen tests)

Thanks — I’ve looped in security@ciso.nexahealth.com for technical follow-up.

Logan / team —

We can support Nexa's request. Summary of what we can provide immediately and policy notes: 

What we can provide now
- Executive pen test summary (redwood-pen-summary-2026.pdf) — suitable for procurement review (redacted; no PII or detailed exploit PoC).
- Vulnerability SLA definitions (see attached redwood-vuln-sladefinitions.md).
- Current scan snapshot (scan-snapshot-20270614.csv) showing last internal weekly scans and most recent external scans.

Pen-test / disclosure policy (high-level)
- Third-party pentest cadence: annually (external) + quarterly automated external scans; internal dynamic scans run weekly.
- Handback & disclosure: We provide an executive summary publicly. Full third-party report can be shared under an MSA/NDA and limited-access link to authorized contacts (security@ciso.nexahealth.com).

Vulnerability SLA (recommended for RFP)
- Critical: initial response within 24 hours, mitigation plan within 72 hours; advisory to partner and mitigation target within 7 business days where feasible.
- High: initial triage within 48 hours; mitigation or compensating control within 7 business days.
- Medium: triage within 5 business days; remediation in 30 business days (may be slotted by priority).
- Low: standard backlog process and scheduled in next quarterly sprint.

Retest cadence and disclosure windows
- Retest for critical/high issues: we aim for retest within 30 days after mitigation; for medium/low retests scheduled based on release windows.
- Responsible disclosure: 30-day, 60-day, 90-day follow-up pattern for escalating remediation where applicable; we will escalate to execs if a critical item remains open beyond SLA.

Attachments included: redwood-pen-summary-2026.pdf (executive summary), redwood-vuln-sladefinitions.md (SLA + severity matrix), scan-snapshot-20270614.csv (recent scan output).

Let me know if Nexa needs the full report under NDA and we'll route through Legal. I'll also prepare a one-page MOU language suggesting BAA + limited report access for PHI scope.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
